purpose: Structured EDA disaster-economic-recovery ledger linking federal coordination, funding, project composition, implementation capacity, and outcome-measurement limits while preserving local service, firm, household, and political outcomes as open stages.

events.geography: United States; EDA disaster-recovery grant portfolio
events.date_precision: Fiscal years 2014–2024; portfolio aggregate rather than one project date
events.denominator: EDA disaster-recovery grant awards in FY2014–FY2024; award and project denominators differ from communities and residents
events.method: Structured extraction from GAO-26-107742 review of EDA records, Economic Recovery Support Function materials, and grantee outcome reporting
events.missingness: No complete project-level disbursement, completion, place comparison, service-use, firm, worker, household, or resident linkage is retained
events.exposure: EDA awarded about $2.1 billion in disaster-recovery grants during FY2014–FY2024
events.alternatives_before_action: Communities and firms could rely on local funds, private credit, insurance, other federal programs, or delayed recovery; the feasible alternative set is not observed per place or project
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: An award creates a public-investment commitment, but award volume does not establish usable liquidity, completed assets, or timely local benefit
events.choice_or_response: EDA and grantees selected projects and implementation paths; local governments, firms, workers, and residents are not linked to individual award decisions
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Congress, EDA, and grantees control appropriations, awards, project design, and implementation; affected residents have no observed control over portfolio allocation
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Grant awards are an institutional response to disaster-economic disruption, not a verified repair, employment, or household remedy
events.immediate_outcome: Federal investment scale is visible as an aggregate capacity endpoint
events.protected_outcome: Some funded projects may improve infrastructure, facilities, or business capacity; no protected community or household outcome is retained
events.sacrificed_outcome: Unfunded, delayed, or poorly measured places may carry continued service, employment, or business risk; the portfolio does not identify them reliably
events.cost_risk_transfer: Portfolio allocation and implementation delays can leave local governments, firms, workers, and residents carrying recovery costs despite aggregate federal awards
events.later_outcome: Project completion, usable service, firm survival, jobs, wages, household access, resilience, trust, and political action remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: No resident or firm-level attribution, fairness judgment, legitimacy, or trust change is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: Agency and grantee reporting are visible; resident organizing, public input, or political action is not
events.counterexample: A large award portfolio can coexist with delayed implementation or unmeasured local outcomes; awards are not recovery
events.source_and_uncertainty: GAO-26-107742; portfolio aggregates and audit findings do not identify a causal community recovery effect

events.geography: United States; Economic Recovery Support Function missions
events.date_precision: 2013–2025 mission period; individual mission start and completion dates are not retained
events.denominator: 45 Economic Recovery Support Function missions; mission duration and community outcome denominators differ
events.method: Structured extraction from GAO-26-107742 review of EDA coordination records
events.missingness: No mission-level project completion, local capacity, service availability, firm, job, household, or resident outcome linkage is retained
events.exposure: EDA coordinated 45 Economic Recovery Support Function missions during 2013–2025, with a median mission length of about five months
events.alternatives_before_action: Communities could coordinate through state/local systems, other federal channels, nonprofits, or ad hoc arrangements; comparative coordination routes are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Coordination can reduce fragmented federal response, but a mission count and duration do not establish timely implementation or local usefulness
events.choice_or_response: EDA and 13 participating agencies coordinated support functions; local actors' uptake and ability to implement recommendations are not retained
events.person_or_actor_with_control: EDA and participating agencies control federal coordination; state/local actors control much of delivery and implementation
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: A mission is an institutional coordination response, not a completed asset, service restoration, or economic recovery outcome
events.immediate_outcome: Federal coordination capacity is observable as a distinct stage between disaster and project implementation
events.protected_outcome: Some communities may receive coordinated technical or funding support; no place-level protected outcome is verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Communities outside an active mission or with low local capacity may face coordination gaps; distribution is not measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: Weak or delayed coordination can shift planning and administrative burdens onto local governments and affected firms
events.later_outcome: Awards, disbursement, completion, services, jobs, wages, household security, trust, and political action remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: No local resident or firm-level judgment of coordination fairness or legitimacy is observed
events.public_or_collective_response: Interagency coordination is observed; local participation and collective action are not
events.counterexample: A five-month median mission does not imply equal capacity, speed, or success across disasters or places
events.source_and_uncertainty: GAO-26-107742; mission counts and durations do not establish project or community effects

events.geography: United States; EDA disaster supplemental funding and selected Hawaii recovery accounts
events.date_precision: FY2018–FY2025 appropriations and selected stakeholder reports; exact project disbursement dates are not retained
events.denominator: EDA disaster supplemental appropriations and selected Hawaii stakeholder accounts; not a national project-delay denominator
events.method: Structured extraction from GAO-26-107742 review of appropriations, EDA records, and stakeholder evidence
events.missingness: No project-level award-to-disbursement interval, place counterfactual, lost output, firm, worker, household, or resident linkage is retained
events.exposure: Congress provided EDA about $3.2 billion in disaster supplemental appropriations in FY2018–FY2025; Hawaii stakeholders reported supplemental funds arriving about two years after the disaster
events.alternatives_before_action: Local governments and firms could use insurance, credit, local revenues, other grants, or delay projects; actual substitution and financing costs are not observed
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Appropriation creates potential fiscal capacity, while delayed availability can constrain planning and implementation during the recovery window
events.choice_or_response: EDA, Congress, and grantees managed authorization, rules, awards, and project timing; the retained evidence does not identify a specific delayed project outcome
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Congress and federal agencies control funding authority and rules; grantees control project administration within those constraints
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Supplemental appropriation and eventual funding are institutional responses, but they are not proof of timely liquidity or completed recovery
events.immediate_outcome: Funding availability and timing are separated as distinct public-capacity stages
events.protected_outcome: Some projects may receive usable funds in time to support recovery; no project-level protection is verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Selected stakeholders reported planning and implementation burdens from delayed funds; national magnitude and downstream effects are unknown
events.cost_risk_transfer: Funding delay can shift bridge-financing, lost-activity, and administrative risks to local governments, firms, workers, and residents
events.later_outcome: Project completion, local output, jobs, wages, services, household access, trust, and political action remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: Stakeholder accounts identify delay concerns but do not measure broad legitimacy, fairness, or trust change
events.public_or_collective_response: Stakeholder reporting is visible; no linked public action or collective response is retained
events.counterexample: A reported Hawaii delay does not establish that every EDA-funded place experienced the same timing or consequence
events.source_and_uncertainty: GAO-26-107742; selected stakeholder evidence is nongeneralizable and does not quantify lost output or jobs

events.geography: United States; EDA disaster-recovery grant portfolio
events.date_precision: FY2014–FY2024 portfolio composition; individual project completion dates are not retained
events.denominator: EDA disaster-recovery award dollars by project category; category shares are not household or service-use shares
events.method: Structured extraction from GAO-26-107742 reported portfolio composition
events.missingness: No project-level completion, usability, service quality, local price, employment, firm, household, or resident linkage is retained
events.exposure: Nearly 45% of award dollars funded utilities, roadways, and other public infrastructure; another 36% funded business, medical, training, and other facilities
events.alternatives_before_action: Places could repair through local funds, private investment, insurance, other programs, or delayed construction; the portfolio does not observe alternative provision per project
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Project category indicates intended capacity investment, not a verified functioning road, utility, clinic, training site, or business facility
events.choice_or_response: EDA and grantees selected project types; resident, customer, worker, and firm use of the resulting assets is not retained
events.person_or_actor_with_control: EDA and grantees control award/project choices, while service users depend on completion, location, affordability, and access
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Infrastructure and facility awards are public responses to disaster-economic need, not verified household or firm remedies
events.immediate_outcome: The distribution of intended investment across infrastructure and facilities is observed
events.protected_outcome: Some projects may restore or add capacity; no user-level protected service or economic outcome is verified
events.sacrificed_outcome: Projects that are delayed, unusable, inaccessible, or poorly matched may leave local needs unmet; portfolio data do not identify them
events.cost_risk_transfer: Investment choices can distribute maintenance, access, and implementation risks across governments, firms, workers, and residents
events.later_outcome: Usable service, firm openings/closures, jobs, wages, prices, migration, household access, trust, and political action remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: No community-level fairness, legitimacy, or trust change is measured
events.public_or_collective_response: Project selection and reporting are visible; public participation and collective action are not
events.counterexample: A project category and award amount do not establish that an asset was completed, usable, affordable, or equitably accessed
events.source_and_uncertainty: GAO-26-107742; award composition is not an implementation or impact measure

events.geography: United States; EDA disaster-recovery grants with available three-year reporting
events.date_precision: GAO review of FY2014–FY2024 awards and available three-year reports
events.denominator: 292 construction and revolving-loan grants with available reported three-year outcomes; not all awards and not independently validated outcomes
events.method: Structured extraction from GAO-26-107742 audit of EDA performance measures and grantee-reported outcomes
events.missingness: No validated project outcomes, comparable place counterfactual, resident access, household security, worker trajectory, or political response is retained
events.exposure: Among 292 grants with available data, 55% of grantees reported no jobs created or retained and no private investment after three years; GAO found the grantee data insufficiently reliable for estimating economic effects
events.alternatives_before_action: Grantees could report other service, infrastructure, firm, or community outcomes; the retained performance system does not establish which outcomes were omitted or independently verified
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: The measurement system supplies a bounded reported outcome but cannot validate whether intended economic effects occurred
events.choice_or_response: EDA used grantee reporting and had suspended validation steps for grantee-reported job data; no independent corrective sequence is retained
events.person_or_actor_with_control: EDA controls performance requirements and validation; grantees generate reports; affected communities and residents are not represented as outcome reporters
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: Performance reporting is an accountability response, but the measurement limitation leaves project success and failure unresolved
events.immediate_outcome: A measurement gap is documented as a governance endpoint rather than converted into a failure rate
events.protected_outcome: Some grants may have produced jobs, private investment, or other benefits not captured by the bounded measure
events.sacrificed_outcome: Some intended outcomes may not have occurred or may remain unverified; the audit cannot distinguish these possibilities
events.cost_risk_transfer: Weak validation can transfer uncertainty and accountability costs to communities, policymakers, and future funding decisions
events.later_outcome: Validated economic function, household benefit, resilience, trust, and political action remain open
events.meaning_and_attribution: No resident or firm-level judgment of program legitimacy or fairness is measured
events.public_or_collective_response: Audit and grantee reporting are observed; public response and later policy action are not
events.counterexample: The 55% reported outcome is not a 55% failure rate: grants with missing or unvalidated outcomes and other benefits remain possible
events.source_and_uncertainty: GAO-26-107742; denominator is 292 grants with available data, and GAO cautions that grantee reports cannot support economic-effect estimates

arrows.evidence: EDA awards, Economic Recovery Support Function missions, and supplemental appropriations establish public inputs while GAO identifies staffing, guidance, and timing constraints
arrows.counterexample: Public inputs can coexist with delayed or incomplete local implementation; no same-place causal estimate is retained
arrows.remaining_gap: Place-keyed award, disbursement, completion, staffing, and usable-service records

arrows.to: usable infrastructure, facility, or firm capacity
arrows.evidence: Portfolio composition identifies infrastructure and facility investment categories, but the review does not validate completion or local function
arrows.counterexample: Award dollars and category shares do not prove a functioning asset, service, job, or household benefit
arrows.remaining_gap: Project completion, service availability, firm use, jobs/wages, prices, and customer/resident access

arrows.evidence: GAO reports selected funding delays and that current measures cannot reliably assess intended economic outcomes
arrows.counterexample: Unmeasured or delayed outcomes are not proof of failed recovery or harm in every place
arrows.remaining_gap: Comparable local counterfactual, validated outcomes, implementation dates, and distributional incidence

arrows.to: household security, trust, or political action
arrows.evidence: The GAO framework identifies intended economic and community outcomes, but retained records contain no linked resident, household, or political follow-up
arrows.counterexample: Visible public investment may improve capacity without changing trust, while delayed or uneven benefits may matter politically; neither path is observed here
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-place resident/customer access, household security, attribution, trust, complaint, political action, and later resilience

boundary: This ledger formalizes a bounded EDA disaster-economic-recovery route from federal coordination and funding through project composition and measurement limits. It does not claim that awards caused or failed to cause local jobs, services, household recovery, trust, or political action.
storage_boundary: No full grant archive, project file, resident microdata, or independent outcome panel is retained; only bounded GAO-reported stages, denominators, uncertainty, source URL, and open arrows are represented.
